beats.role_note: COLD OPEN LAW — Claude UI cold open. Ask lands answered; narration introduces Liam in for Bear.
beats.narration_text: Namaste, this is Liam, in for Bear. Every fellow in Brutalist has typed dot slash art help. What most people miss is that four different aliases hit that same line, and the help text you see is not stored anywhere. It is the file's own header, extracted by sed at run time. Here is what that means, and where it stops.

props.command: What does ./art help actually do — and what does it not do?
output: prints a 17-line usage sheet, then exits 0
four aliases fire it: empty, -h, --help, help

beats.role_note: EXECUTIVE-SUMMARY LAW — Beat 2 BLUF, written by the hesitant writer. Corrects the reel's actual misconception.
beats.narration_text: Watch the writer walk this back. Art help does not list every skill. It prints every command, straight from the file's own header. The skills catalog is a different command.

beats.role_note: FRAMEWORK — the shape of the dispatcher. Bash case, one branch per alias.
beats.narration_text: The whole toolkit is one bash script called art. Inside is a single case statement — one branch per command. The very first branch matches four patterns with pipes between them: empty string, dash h, dash dash help, and the word help. All four aliases hit the same body.

show.event: code card fades in with 'art' in the title bar
'case "$cmd" in' types
four alias patterns type on the same line
body of the branch (sed pipe) types under it
spark line settles under the card

props.title: art — the dispatcher (bash)
props.sparkLine: One dispatcher. One branch per command.

beats.role_note: MECHANISM — how the help text is generated. Not stored; extracted from the file's own header.
beats.narration_text: This is the whole body. Two sed calls. The first grabs lines two through eighteen of the art file itself. The second strips the leading hash and space that make those lines a shell comment. What you see on your terminal is the file reading its own head, without the hash marks.

show.event: code card in; title reads 'art:39 — the help body'
sed line types character by character
comment underneath types: '# reads its own header'
spark line lands

props.title: art:56 — the help body
props.code:
# One line. Two sed calls. That is the whole implementation.
sed -n '2,18p' "$ART_HOME/art" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'

# 1st sed: print lines 2..18 of the art file itself.
# 2nd sed: strip the leading '# ' (or '#') from each line.
# Net effect: the file's own header, un-commented, is the help.
props.sparkLine: The help IS the header, minus the hash.

beats.role_note: WORKED EXAMPLE — the actual output captured from this workspace, verbatim.
beats.narration_text: So this is what runs. Seventeen lines. The first line is a title. The other sixteen are commands, each with a short description. There are no colours, no pager, no interactive prompt. It prints, it exits zero, it is done.

props.title: $ ./art help  (verbatim, 17 lines)
props.code:
art — one entry point for the brutalist toolkit (the pared-down brutalist-art).

  ./art --list                 list the skills
  ./art <skill> --help         show a skill's SKILL.md
  ./art scenes "<beat need>"   LIBRARY-FIRST scene search — run BEFORE authoring a beat
  ./art scenes --check <Name>  is that composition renderable? (the anti-slate check)
  ./art scene-index            regenerate scenes.json + SCENE-DOC-TODO.md after adding one
  ./art icons "<what it needs>" CANONICAL icon search — run BEFORE drawing a mark
  ./art icons --check <name>   is that icon in the set? (the anti-redraw check)
  ./art icon-build             re-cut the canonical set from svg/ (rarely needed)
  ./art todo  <reel> [flags]   per-video beat ledger (which beats need filling, how)
  ./art run   <reel> [flags]   compile a review cut
  ./art shorts <reel> [flags]  derive the 9:16 Short (cap check + auto-shorten)
  ./art vertical <reel>        full-length 9:16 companion (no shortening)
  ./art approvals <reel> --fingerprints  inspect human-review subjects (never signs)
  ./art final <reel>           verified master — no review label (→ <slug>.mp4)
  ./art doctor                 dependency readiness (wraps ./setup)

$  # exit 0  (smoke + keys exist at header lines 19-20, not shown — beyond sed 2,18p range)
props.sparkLine: 17 lines. Exits 0. (smoke + keys beyond sed range)

beats.role_note: MECHANISM — the four aliases share one body.
beats.narration_text: The alias set is the interesting part. Bash pipes inside a case pattern mean this branch matches four different things. The empty string, so bare dot slash art matches. Dash h. Dash dash help. And the literal word help. All four hit the same sed line. Same output, no duplicated code.

show.event: card in; title reads 'the four aliases'
four invocations type as a grid
arrow annotation ties them to the '""|-h|--help|help)' pattern
spark line lands

props.title: the four aliases → one branch
props.code:
# All four print the SAME 17-line usage sheet:
$ ./art               # empty string alias
$ ./art -h            # short flag
$ ./art --help        # long flag
$ ./art help          # bare word

# The case pattern that catches them, in art:55 :
""|-h|--help|help)
    sed -n '2,18p' "$ART_HOME/art" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'
    ;;

beats.narration_text: Now the near miss. Dot slash art dash dash list is a different command. It is not an alias for help. It prints the skills table — every skill in the toolkit with a one-line role. If you want the commands, use help. If you want the skills, use dash dash list. They cover different scopes.

show.event: card in; title reads '$ ./art --list'
skills table types, first 8 rows
footer annotation: 'commands vs skills — different scopes'

beats.role_note: FALSIFIABILITY — a real failure. Unknown command does NOT print help; it exits 2 with one line.
beats.narration_text: And here is what a wrong guess actually does. Dot slash art bogus does not print help. It falls through the case into the star branch and exits with status two. One line to standard error, pointing you at dash dash list. This is the recovery hint that keeps you from typing help six different ways.

show.event: card in; title reads '$ ./art bogus'
one-line error appears in terracotta
'echo $?  # 2' types below
spark line lands

props.title: $ ./art bogus   (the failure path)
props.code:
$ ./art bogus
art: unknown skill 'bogus' (try ./art --list)
$ echo $?
2

# From art:127-129 — the fall-through case:
*)
  dir="$(skill_dir "$cmd")"
  [ -z "$dir" ] && { echo "art: unknown skill '$cmd' (try ./art --list)"; exit 2; }
  # …
  ;;
props.sparkLine: Not the help. Exit 2. Points to --list.

beats.role_note: RECOVERY — how to get from a wrong guess to the right thing in two commands.
beats.narration_text: The recovery is two commands. Dot slash art dash dash list shows every skill by name. Then dot slash art followed by the skill name and dash dash help opens that skill's SKILL dot m-d in your pager. So the arc is: help for commands, dash dash list for skills, skill dash dash help for a specific one. Three commands cover the whole surface.

show.event: card in; title reads 'the recovery path'
line 1 types: ./art --list
line 2 types: ./art fellows --help
comment types under: '# opens SKILL.md in $PAGER (defaults to cat)'

props.title: wrong guess → recovery in two commands
props.code:
# 1. See every skill (name + one-line role):
$ ./art --list

# 2. Open one skill's SKILL.md in your pager:
$ ./art fellows --help
$ ./art ai-explainer --help
$ ./art your-turn --help

# From art:130-132 — that's a second '--help' path:
if [ "${1:-}" = "--help" ] || [ "${1:-}" = "-h" ]; then
  exec "${PAGER:-cat}" "$dir/SKILL.md"
fi

# Whole surface, three commands:
#   help          → commands
#   --list        → skills
#   <skill> --help → that skill's SKILL.md

beats.role_note: VERDICT — the split. Four scopes, in order.
beats.narration_text: So the split. Art help is the 17-line command sheet, pulled from the file's own header. Dash dash list is the skills table. Skill dash dash help is that skill's SKILL dot m-d. An unknown token is exit two, one line, pointing at dash dash list. Four scopes, one dispatcher, zero surprises.

beats.role_note: HANDOFF LAW — Your Turn composer. Prompt read aloud verbatim, then discussed.
beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude Code from the brutalist toolkit root. Ask Claude to run each alias, capture the output, diff them line by line, then confirm the exit codes. What you should see is four identical outputs, four zero exit codes, and one unknown token that exits two. If any pair differs, you have found a bug — file it against the case block at art line 38.

props.command: From the brutalist.art toolkit root, run each of these and compare: ./art, ./art -h, ./art --help, ./art help, ./art bogus. Save stdout for each to /tmp/art-<alias>.txt, capture $? into the same file, then diff every pair of the first four. Report: any diff, any non-zero exit for the first four, and the exit code + stderr line for bogus. Confirm the fifth exits 2 and points at --list.
output: one exit code of 2 for bogus, stderr line points to --list
